title: feat(service-print): print a record's print page to a PDF in headless Chromium as the requesting user, and archive it on the record
body:
Fixes #22269

Clause-②: yes (widening)

Print page ③ of the B′ split: `@objectstack/service-print`, a render service with one engine (headless Chromium) that renders a record's print page under the requesting user's own principal and archives the PDF, as that user, as a `sys_file` attached to the record. It builds on the landed `file-attachments` archive, which it widens with a caller-scoped face, and binds to the principal-session mint of the seam card objectstack-ai/objectstack#23772.

**Binding state: bound.** #23772 has landed (PR #23786), and so has the fix that lets a minted session boot the console (#23813). The service reads `IAuthService.mintPrincipalSession` through ONE package-local adapter, `packages/services/service-print/src/principal-session.ts` (`principalSessionMinterOf`), which is typed by the contract's own `IAuthService` and `PrincipalSession`. `status()` reports `unavailable`, naming that member, only where the composed auth service does not offer it.

## What it adds

- **`PrintServicePlugin`** registers the in-process `print` service (`IPrintService`): `status()` and `printRecordToFile({ app, object, recordId, page, filename? }, context)`. Explicit composition; no route, no metadata key, no error code, no `requires` token.
- **One engine, two placements** (ruling of record on this card, OQ5 → B):
  - local: `OS_PRINT_CHROMIUM_PATH` / `chromiumPath`. Per render, `chromium.launchServer({ executablePath, headless: true })` and `chromium.connect` to it, one browser process per render. Disposal closes the connection, then the server, and kills the process if a close does not settle within 2 s;
  - remote: `OS_PRINT_BROWSER_ENDPOINT` / `browserEndpoint`, a DevTools WebSocket endpoint, `chromium.connectOverCDP` per render. Its context closes first, then the connection, each bounded the same way;
  - both need `OS_PRINT_CONSOLE_URL` / `consoleUrl`, the console URL that browser reaches (`/_console` included). A console URL carrying credentials (`user:password@`) is refused, and so is configuring both placements at once; each is reported as misconfigured.
  - `playwright-core` `1.63.0`, pinned exact on this package only (already in the lockfile).
- **Loud at `start()`**:
  - the plugin probes the engine (launch or connect, read the version, close) and logs the placement and Chromium version;
  - an absent, misconfigured or unreachable engine is one `warn` naming the setting;
  - `status()` reports `ready | unconfigured | misconfigured | unavailable` with the reason;
  - the plugin never logs the remote endpoint or the console URL beyond scheme and host, and `status()` never shows more: the endpoint may carry a token, and a value that does not parse is described as unparseable, never echoed.
- **`ICallerFileAttachmentService`** (`@objectstack/service-storage`, exported type, `minor`): the `file-attachments` service's caller-scoped face, on the same slot and the same one writer. `IFileAttachmentService` and `attachFile` are unchanged.
  - `assertMayAttach(parentObject, parentId, context)` throws the insert's own refusal without writing:
    - `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403 when `ISecurityService.explain` says the caller may not create `sys_attachment`;
    - `ATTACHMENT_PARENT_ACCESS` / 403 when the attach rule (parent EDIT) refuses.
  - `attachFileAs(input, context)`:
    - writes one `sys_file` owned by the caller, and one `sys_attachment` inserted under the caller's own context, so every insert gate judges the caller and `uploaded_by` is stamped;
    - acts in the caller's organization only: an `organizationId` other than the context's `tenantId` (or `null` when it names none) is `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403, before anything is read or written.
  - A system or user-less context is refused `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403 on both verbs.
- **Refusals, in the ruled order, all before any mint or launch.** Each pin asserts `code` + `status`, and that mint, render and archive were never called:

  | # | condition | code / status |
  |:--|:--|:--|
  | 1 | not a human user acting for themselves (no context, system, agent/service/guest/system kind, an `authGate` hold) | `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403 |
  | 2 | engine not `ready` (unconfigured, misconfigured — e.g. both placements, or a console URL with credentials — never probed, or a service a print needs not composed) | `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` / 503 |
  | 3 | unknown page | `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` / 404 |
  | 3 | a malformed request field; a page of another object, no `print`, or not the object's default record page | `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400 |
  | 4 | record read AS THE CALLER returns nothing, or the read is refused 403 | `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` / 404 |
  | 5 | object without `enable: { files: true }` | `FILES_DISABLED` / 403 |
  | 5 | the caller may not create attachments (`assertMayAttach`) | `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403 |
  | 5 | the caller may not attach to this record: the attach rule, parent EDIT (`assertMayAttach`) | `ATTACHMENT_PARENT_ACCESS` / 403 |

  An engine whose last probe failed, with every service composed, is probed once more only after step 5. If that probe fails too, the answer is `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` / 503. So no browser is launched or connected before any of the refusals above.
- **Then:**
  - mint (TTL 60 s, twice the 30 s render budget, under the contract's 120 s ceiling);
  - render: one 30 s deadline over every step, from open to `page.pdf`, so a stall answers `TIMEOUT` / 504; the cleanup after it is bounded, and a browser that arrives late is closed;
  - archive: `attachFileAs` as the caller;
  - **revoke in `finally`** (pinned after a failed render and after a refused archive).
  - A revoke that itself fails never replaces the print's outcome. It is logged at `error` on the plugin's logger, naming the user and a 12-hex fingerprint of the session (never the token or the cookie), and the 60 s TTL ends the session (pinned through the plugin).
- **The page binding**: the browser loads `CONSOLE/apps/APP/OBJECT/record/ID` with the minted cookie, waits for the print root (`data-print-page`) AND `window.__objectui.idle` for 3 consecutive polls, then `document.fonts.ready`, then `page.pdf({ preferCSSPageSize: true })` — the print keys are mapped to CSS once, by the console.
- **Showcase**: `showcase_invoice_document`, the invoice's default record page, declares `print`; `showcase_invoice` declares `enable: { files: true }`. Section headings and the page label are translated (en, zh-CN).
- Docs:
  - `content/docs/ui/print-pages.mdx` (+ the ui landing row);
  - the `OS_PRINT_*` rows in `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`;
  - the `packages.mdx` row;
  - README and changeset.

## Measured (mechanism assumptions)

1. **The archive.** Built on the `file-attachments` writer as it is, run AS THE CALLER through `attachFileAs`; there is no second archive entry, and no `IFileAttachmentService` or `packages/spec` change.
   - The caller-scoped refusal chain runs before any mint or launch: the record read with the caller's own context (`RECORD_NOT_FOUND`), the `FILES_DISABLED` pre-check, and `assertMayAttach`.
   - **The earlier gap is fixed.** On a real showcase boot, attaching under the system context had left `sys_file.owner_id` and `sys_attachment.uploaded_by` null and skipped the parent-EDIT gate. Both rows now name the requester, and the attach rule judges them. This is pinned on a real showcase boot (`print-service-archive.dogfood.test.ts`, and the real render in `print-service-render.dogfood.test.ts`).
   - A reader who may read every invoice but edit none is refused `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403 before any mint or render.
2. **The page binding at `.objectui-sha` `f96f771140`**, re-read at `daeb77fc84dd`, the pin at this head.
   - The console renders a record ONLY on its bound page: the object's default record page, else the first record page. No URL renders a named, non-default page for a record (`RecordDetailView` calls `usePageAssignment(objectName)` without `pageName`, `RecordDetailView.tsx:640` at the pin).
   - The print root marker exists: `PageRenderer` stamps `data-print-page` on a print page.
   - **Measured end to end** with the console built at the pin, my driver, both placements, and a normally signed-in session. The invoice print page renders on A4 with its details, line-items table, Chinese header and footer, and page number (`pdfinfo`: 1 page, 594.96 x 841.92 pts; fonts include `WenQuanYiZenHei`). The run through the service itself with a minted session is item 3.
   - Missing surface (objectui): a route that renders a named print page for a record.
3. **The mint (#23772) against the real console: boots, after #23813.**
   - Before that fix, a minted session kept the console on "Opening your console…". The measured difference was that the short session was renewed on every `get-session` read.
   - With the fix merged (`0cfd0c49bd`), `print-service-render.dogfood.test.ts` prints through the service's own path, with a session minted by `IAuthService.mintPrincipalSession`, against the console built at `daeb77fc84dd`, on both placements. It asserts:
     - the console booted as the requester;
     - both rows name the requester;
     - the minted session answers 401 after the print, after a success and after a forced failure.
   - Green 6/6 at `9252cd175e`, and again at `78e50355a2` after the round-3 driver changes.
4. **The driver library.**
   - Local: `launchServer({ executablePath })` + `connect`. Remote: `connectOverCDP(endpoint)`. Both work on Chromium 141.
   - Closing a CDP-connected browser leaves the remote browser running, and its render context (and cookie) gone (pinned).
   - The injected-launcher pins hold the bounded cleanup, with no browser: a close that never settles still answers within the budget plus the grace, and the local process is killed; an open that settles after the deadline is closed and never given a context.
5. **The CJK pin**: text extraction cannot tell glyphs from boxes (`pdftotext` returns the Chinese text from a tofu render). The pin asserts every Chinese code point is a ToUnicode target of an embedded font. Ablation (Chromium narrowed to a Latin-only fontconfig, no code change), both placements red: `expected [ '发', '票', '客', '户', '名', '称', …(12) ] to deeply equal []`; restored green.

## Tests

- **`@objectstack/service-print`: 79 tests.**
  - config: both placements, misconfiguration, redaction, a console URL with credentials or one that does not parse;
  - service: every refusal, the order, the deferred re-probe, mint/render/archive/revoke, a failed revoke, the caller's own context, no credential in a message;
  - the driver with an injected launcher: the cookie redaction, one budget over every step, the bounded cleanup, a late open;
  - plugin `start()` loudness against a missing executable and a dead endpoint carrying a token, and the plugin-level revoke-log pin;
  - the real-Chromium engine on both placements: render as the session, A4 from `@page`, the CJK pin, timeout → `TIMEOUT` / 504, remote cleanup.
  - The Chromium file runs where `OS_TEST_PRINT_CHROMIUM_PATH` or `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH/chromium` exists, and says it was skipped otherwise.
- **`@objectstack/service-storage`: 1029 tests**, including the caller-face pins against a real ObjectQL engine and its insert gates:
  - the system context refused on both verbs;
  - `owner_id` / `uploaded_by` = the caller;
  - `ATTACHMENT_PARENT_ACCESS` from the real insert gate;
  - `PERMISSION_DENIED` from `explain`;
  - `FILES_DISABLED` as the caller;
  - another organization refused.
- **`packages/qa/dogfood/test/print-service-archive.dogfood.test.ts`: 9 tests.**
  - The plugin as composed on a real showcase boot: unconfigured status, 503, 403.
  - The service over the real kernel services: unknown page 404; non-print page 400; another user's invoice hidden by RLS 404 (with a caller/system control); a reader who cannot attach, 403; a successful archive as one committed `sys_file` + one `sys_attachment` on the invoice, both naming the requester; the real mint revoked at the wire.
- **`packages/qa/dogfood/test/print-service-render.dogfood.test.ts`: 6 tests**, 3 per placement. The real render through the real console with a minted session, as Measured 3 describes.
  - It needs a built Console and a Chromium, and says it was skipped otherwise.
- These counts are the dev's runs: 79 and 1029 at `5a16f29db9`; 9 and 6 at `78e50355a2`. In CI the two Chromium-gated files skip, and the dogfood suite runs only in main's full battery.

## Acceptance notes

- `packages/spec/liveness`'s `page.print` row was flipped from `planned` to `live` on `main` before this head (PR #23776, closing #23710). The finding first noted here is resolved, and needs no spec-lane follow-up.
- Observed on the real PDF, and routed at ACCEPT (the seat record on this PR):
  - The record details' "Show N empty fields" toggle reaches paper. This is card ② print rendering, an objectui follow-up.
  - Line-item column headings print field names rather than labels. That is not a renderer defect: `record:line_items` draws a column exactly as declared, and does not hydrate a label from the child field (`packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts:2494`). The showcase page's columns declare no `label`, so the follow-up is in this repo's showcase.
- The CJK pin measures the browser's host fonts; a local placement without a CJK font prints boxes. The docs page says so.

## Surface deviations (declared)

- `packages/spec/llms.txt`: the package count 71 → 72, forced by the new package (`check:llms-txt`), with a `@objectstack/spec` patch line in the changeset. No other `packages/spec` change.
- `turbo.json` and `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs`: the dogfood tests' declared inputs gain `packages/services/service-print/src/**` and `packages/console/dist/index.html`, the latter with `heldBy` (`check:cross-package-test-inputs`).
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`: census rows 47d (the print service's system-context refusal) and 47e (the caller-scoped attach verbs' refusal) (`check:system-context-census`).
- `scripts/docs-audit/handwritten-docs.json`: the new docs page (`check:docs-audit-scope`).
- `packages/services/service-storage/src/**`: the caller-scoped face, as REWORK `6208156693` item 2 orders. `storage-service-plugin.ts` and `attachment-access-hooks.ts` were edited only after PR #23767 merged. The hooks change is an extraction of the attach rule's verdict, with behaviour unchanged.
